content.text:
Done. All three flyers are rendered and verified.

**Output** (in the working folder): `portrait.png` 1080×1350, `wide.png` 1200×1000, `sky.png` 300×600 — exact pixel sizes.

**How it's built:** one `template.html` → `build.py` stamps per-size `--s` scale (1 / 0.85 / 0.28) and a crop focal point into `portrait.html`, `wide.html`, `sky.html`. Every type size, padding, gap and icon dimension is `calc(px * var(--s))`, so content scales exactly as specified, while bands (photo, red CTA, navy footer) are laid out at 100% width so they stay full-bleed at any canvas.

**Vertical fit:** the flyer is a flex column; leftover height is distributed proportionally *inside* sections (photo weighted heaviest) rather than pooling into orphan gaps — so the tall 300×600 skyscraper gets a taller hero and airier bands instead of stranded whitespace, and the short 1200×1000 absorbs the deficit by shrinking the photo only.

**Verification** (`check.js`, headless measurement of each real viewport) reports zero problems on all three:
- no overlap between sections, no overflow past the canvas, no gap at the bottom
- no text clipped horizontally or by an overflow-hidden ancestor, nothing out of bounds
- column gaps and widths identical to 0.1px (26/26 portrait, 22.1/22.1 wide, 7.3/7.3 sky)
- photo band, CTA bar and footer confirmed edge-to-edge at every size
- photo uses `object-fit: cover` (1600×900 source, never stretched); focal point tuned per size — 42% portrait (sun + hills), 72% wide (avoids a half-sun sliver on the short band), 50% sky (full height, centered horizontal crop)
- Inter loads via `@font-face` and real variable weights resolve (`document.fonts.check('800 62px Inter')` → true).
